Run all mediation estimators on one synthetic dataset

Source: R/mediation.R
analyze_mediation_robust.Rd

Reference-named entry point: applies UNADJ, DIRECT, COCA, IV2SLS, and PGC (matrix bridge) mediation estimators to each tested outcome feature and returns tidy per-feature results with significance flags for both NDE and NIE. When the dataset includes a mediator instrument (Gm), the 2-stage MR estimator fit_iv2sls_mediation2 (method "IV2SLS2") is also run. When the dataset includes path-specific negative controls (W1, W2;), the two-stage proximal estimator fit_pgc_mediation2 is run as "PGC2" (without Gm) and "PGC2Gm" (with Gm, when Gm is also present).

Usage

analyze_mediation_robust(
  iteration_data,
  test_features = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  n_cores = 1,
  se_method = c("delta", "bootstrap", "composite"),
  n_boot = 500
)

Arguments

iteration_data

Dataset list from run_single_iteration() (or generate_toy_data()). When Gm is present, the 2-stage MR estimator is included.

test_features

Optional integer indices of outcome features to test. Default NULL (all features).

alpha

Significance threshold for the significance flags. Default 0.05.

n_cores

Number of parallel workers. Default 1 (sequential). Uses parallel::mclapply on Unix and a PSOCK cluster on Windows.

se_method

"delta" (default), "bootstrap", or "composite". See iconic_estimate() for details.

n_boot

Number of bootstrap resamples when se_method = "bootstrap". Default 500.

Value

Data frame: feature, method, NDE, NDE_se, NDE_p, NIE, NIE_se, NIE_p, NDE_significant, NIE_significant.

Details

Negative controls are always summarised over the full W panel for COCA, so restricting test_features does not change its control summary. The matrix-bridge PGC uses the full W panel.

A scalar-bridge variant (fit_pgc_scalar_mediation()) is exported for standalone use but is not included in the default pipeline.

Examples

dat <- generate_toy_data(n = 300, mo_confounding = 0.8, seed = 1)
analyze_mediation_robust(dat)
